HARPER-MENDOZA MEDICAL GROUP - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Benjamin Lopez DOB: 05/04/1984 Sex: M MRN: 835115
Admit: 12/21/2024 Discharge: 12/21/2024

Admitting Physician: Dr. Kristina Harris, Oncology

Principal diagnosis: Colon polyp (adenoma), high-grade dysplasia

Secondary diagnosis: None

Hospital course:
Mr. Benjamin Lopez, a 40-year-old male, was seen in the office on December 21, 2024, for follow-up of a colon polyp (adenoma) with high-grade dysplasia, a condition he has been managing since June 1, 2015. The patient has no other significant medical history and his condition remains controlled. 

The patient was last seen on March 8, 2024, where he reported no new symptoms and his vitals were stable with a blood pressure of 131/66 mmHg and a weight of 160 pounds. The physical examination was unremarkable, and routine laboratory tests were within normal limits.

On May 25, 2023, the patient had a follow-up visit where he continued to report no symptoms related to his colon polyp. His blood pressure was recorded at 128/67 mmHg, and his weight was 157 pounds. There were no abnormal findings on physical examination, and all laboratory results were within normal limits.

During his visit on August 10, 2022, the patient had a blood pressure of 139/75 mmHg and weighed 155 pounds. He continued to have no symptoms, and his physical examination and laboratory tests were normal.

On October 26, 2021, the patient had his annual physical examination. His blood pressure was 130/75 mmHg, and his weight was 151 pounds. The examination was unremarkable, and laboratory tests were within normal limits.

The patient's most recent visit prior to this admission was on January 11, 2021, where he reported no symptoms, and blood pressure was 126/78 mmHg with a weight of 159 pounds. The physical examination and laboratory tests were normal.

During this visit on December 21, 2024, the patient's blood pressure was 127/74 mmHg, and he weighed 163 pounds. The physical examination was unremarkable, with no evidence of acute distress. The patient reported no new symptoms and continued to manage his condition well. Routine laboratory tests were ordered and are pending.

Given the stable condition and lack of acute symptoms, the patient was discharged home on the same day. No new medications were prescribed, and the patient was advised to continue with his current management plan.

Discharge medications: None

Discharge instructions:
The patient was instructed to continue with his regular diet and activities. He was advised to follow up with his primary care physician

for routine care and with Dr. Kristina Harris in the Oncology department for continued monitoring of his colon polyp. He was instructed to return to the office if he experiences any new symptoms or if his condition worsens.

Follow-up:
The patient is scheduled for a follow-up appointment in six months to monitor his condition and ensure that his colon polyp remains stable. Routine laboratory tests and possibly a colonoscopy may be recommended at that time to assess for any changes in his condition.

Signature:
